notes:
CIRCUIT: a simple series-parallel AC network. V-AC #2 (4cos20t V) sits in the left rail; the top wire runs right through L#0 (1H) to a node, and from that node R#1 (2ohm) drops to the bottom rail while the top wire also continues right to the right-hand corner and down through C#3 (5uF) to the bottom rail. So R#1 and C#3 are in parallel, and that parallel pair is in series with L#0 across the source. The bottom rail is the reference and carries GND #4. 5 components, 3 nets. (The rectangle around the whole page at x~8..1010, y~283..735 is the scan's page border, not circuit wire; it is an isolated ink group with no terminals and affects nothing.)

NET MAP:
  0  = BOTTOM RAIL / reference: bottom of V-AC #2, bottom of R#1 (2ohm), bottom plate of C#3 (5uF), and GND #4. The horizontal at y~608 from x~150 to x~608 plus the stub down to the GND hatch are all this net.
  n1 = LEFT RAIL TOP: top terminal of V-AC #2, up the left rail and right along the top wire to the left lead of L#0 (1H).
  n2 = TOP NODE: right lead of L#0, the whole top wire from x~350 to the right-hand corner at x~608, the vertical down to the top of R#1 (via site S0), and the vertical down to the top plate of C#3.

CRITICAL SITE DECISIONS:
  S0 (457,352) deg3 -> JUNCTION (agrees with default). Clean T: the top wire arrives from the left, a vertical starts here and runs down to R#1, and the top wire continues to the right toward the capacitor branch. Three branches, all incident, nothing passing over anything; dot=1.5 (ordinary stroke), hop=0.0. A T cannot be a crossing. If this were not joined, R#1 would have a floating top lead and the 2ohm branch would have no path to the source.
  S8 (456,607) deg4 -> JUNCTION (agrees with default, and this is the one load-bearing call on this sheet). The vertical from the bottom of R#1 comes down, CROSSES the bottom rail at y~607, and continues below it into the GND hatch symbol. It is a plain X: dot=1.4 (i.e. no solder blob, just ordinary stroke width) and hop=0.0 (no semicircular hop, no jog). Decided by electrical impossibility (rule 1): under the crossing reading the bottom rail (V-AC bottom + C#3 bottom plate) would be one net and the R#1 bottom + GND another, leaving the 2ohm resistor hanging off the top node with no return path - a one-ended branch, which is impossible. The junction reading also gives the physically expected topology: the bottom rail is the ground reference of the circuit. Rule 2 (ink prior: plain crossing with no hop and no jog is a real junction in this dataset) points the same way. Consequence of the other reading: 4 nets with a stranded resistor.

NON-CRITICAL SITES (all left at default; each is a handwritten-label stroke or a symbol stroke brushing a wire, and none changes the grouping): S1 and S2 = the '1H' caption touching the underside of the inductor coil; S3 = the '2ohm' caption touching R#1's body; S4 and S5 = the '4cos20t V' caption touching the V-AC circle and the left rail; S7 = the '5' of the '5uF' caption touching the capacitor's bottom lead.

PORT FIX:
  #3 Capacitor (5uF): t1 was on p2@(641,479), which is a stroke of the handwritten '5' in the '5uF' caption sitting immediately to the right of the symbol (this is the classic value-label capture, and it showed as the 1-terminal net n3). Repointed t1 to p1@(612,490), the real bottom-plate lead on the vertical wire that runs down to the bottom rail (wire 5). After the fix every net has >= 2 terminals and the ERC is clean.

CLASSES: all five labels match the drawn symbols (circle with a sine inside = V-AC, coil = Inductor, zigzag = Resistor, two parallel horizontal plates = Capacitor, hatch = GND). No reclassification, no unconnected leads, no gap bridges needed dropping (8 bridges, 0 of which change the netlist).
